title: Bijectivity of explicit subset insertion
statement: For every A,r,f,J and integer n as in [def-sc-principal-open-cech-subset-insertion], the explicitly constructed additive insertion map in degree n is bijective. No abstract comparison complex, coordinate isomorphism, differential hypothesis, or augmentation assertion is involved.

source.place: Tag 08C1, equation (20.40.0.1), and Tag 01FM (increasing tuples). Explicit coordinate verification written by V3, following the parent node steps 1 and 2; source read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08C1 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01FM.

proof.text: Construct a reader by totalDesc projection to the subset bidegree, extendXIso, tuple evaluation, and inverse section transport. Prove insertOne(S) followed by readOne(S) is the identity. For S different from T the composite is zero: different bidegrees project to zero, and in equal bidegree their increasing enumerations have different finite ranges, so single-coordinate evaluation vanishes. Sum these identities to prove reading insertion is coordinate evaluation; insertion is injective. All calculations and equal-bidegree transports are proved by private Lean helpers.

Use the coproduct universal property to identify each total term with the direct sum of its bidegree components (Mathlib ModuleCat.coproductCoconeIsColimit). DirectSum.induction_on reduces membership in the additive range of insertion to each bidegree summand; the range contains zero and is closed under addition. Negative first degree is zero by extension by zero. In nonnegative first degree p, extendXIso and Finset.univ_sum_single reduce to one tuple coordinate. If no increasing tuple exists (in particular p>=r), the finite sum is empty.

For a tuple t take its finite image S. Its cardinality is p+1, and orderEmbOfFin_unique proves its increasing enumeration is t. The total-degree equation forces the coefficient degree to n+1-card(S). Insert the coordinate family supported at S, with value the inverse section transport of the given tuple section. Expanding the finite insertion sum leaves only S, and section transport cancels its inverse. This is exactly the given tuple generator, so every total element lies in the range and insertion is surjective. Combine with injectivity. The same induction handles r=0, empty or repeated opens, and zero section groups.
